text: Yes, there was tree-cover loss on the property in 2020. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset detected a 0.7-hectare loss, which meets the minimum event size threshold of 0.5 hectares. The European Commission’s JRC 2020 reference data corroborated this, confirming that 100% of the affected area was forested at the time. The Uruguayan MGAP forest map identified the lost area as planted forest (Pinus species), not native forest. While additional small patches (1.3 hectares) were lost in 2020, these were below the detection threshold and not counted as part of the event. The loss represents 0.02% of the total asset area.
